## 07 创 Map in. Traps out. · 地图进，布点出

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/enterprise/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/enterprise/

First-passage maths becomes a product prototype: BioPath takes a site map and a budget, proposes trap locations and supplies a reproducible model-comparison report. The enterprise journey includes an Early Career Enterprise Fellowship, a New Enterprise pitch award and a Festival of Enterprise PechaKucha.

_Fig. 7 — How trap placement changes expected capture time in a model field._

- 23 Dec 2025 · **Early Career Enterprise Fellow, 2026** (2026 年早期职业创业学者) — Awarded. An application on 11 December 2025 proposed BioPath, ‘a bio-inspired optimisation tool for precision pest management’ that turns first-passage research into trap-placement software. On 23 December the university's enterprise leadership sent a successful outcome, and the fellowship was accepted the same day — one of twelve Early Career Enterprise Fellows in the 2026 cohort. Metrics: Fellows in the 2026 cohort 12.
- 6 Jan 2026 – 2 Mar 2026 · **New Enterprise: a first pitch award** (New Enterprise：第一个路演奖) — Awarded. Accepted onto the Careers Service start-up programme New Enterprise: DEVELOPMENT in January 2026; then weekly workshops, a pitch on 24 February in the Wills Memorial Building, and a £150 award for BioPath on 2 March 2026 — a small first win on the road from theorem to product. Metrics: Award £150.
- 20 Feb 2026 – 1 Jun 2026 · **Learning to pitch in twenty slides** (学会用二十页讲完) — Completed. The fellowship came with a training programme run with the university's enterprise partner — building a team, funding and investment — and two rounds of PechaKucha coaching, in May online and in June in person, ahead of the Festival of Enterprise. PechaKucha is unforgiving: twenty slides, twenty seconds each, no going back.
- 23 Feb 2026 · **The BioPath platform: map in, traps out, comparisons attached** (BioPath 平台：地图进，布点出，附比较报告) — Live. The software behind the fellowship: a Python platform with a command-line tool, an API and a static pitch site. It takes a site map and a monitoring budget and proposes trap or sensor coordinates under a first-passage model. The reproducible report compares the optimised score with heuristic and random baselines, includes a robust worst-case score and records the Monte Carlo runs behind them. These are model comparisons, not a guarantee of field performance. An automated benchmark loop has pushed nearly two thousand benchmark commits on its own, and the pitch site is live. Links: [Pitch site](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/biopath-platform/) · [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/biopath-platform)
- 26 Feb 2026 · **Introduced as a 2026 Enterprise Fellow** (作为 2026 届创业学者被介绍) — Featured. The university's Enterprise & Innovation blog introduced the 2026 cohort of Early Career Enterprise Fellows on 26 February 2026, including a statement on BioPath: a software tool for more precise and sustainable pest management on farms and grain-storage sites, aiming to cut reliance on chemical rodenticides. The post was also featured in that day's bulletin. Links: [E&I blog post](https://enterpriseinnovation.blogs.bristol.ac.uk/2026/02/26/introducing-the-2026-early-career-enterprise-fellows/)
- 5 Mar 2026 – 15 Jun 2026 · **New Enterprise: GROWTH** (New Enterprise：GROWTH 阶段) — Completed. After the development award, BioPath moved on to the New Enterprise: GROWTH 2025/26 cohort — a series of masterclasses through the spring and a mentor from the university's research and commercialisation team, matched in late March 2026.
- 10 Jun 2026 · **PechaKucha at the Festival of Enterprise** (创业节上的 PechaKucha) — Presented. Presented BioPath as a twenty-slide PechaKucha at the University of Bristol Festival of Enterprise in the Arts Complex on 10 June 2026, with a printed poster for the showcase and a one-line promise: ‘Map in. Traps out. Proof attached.’ The talk also lives as a web deck, and that same night an 8 min 58 s pitch video was cut with 135 burned-in bilingual subtitle cues, transcribed by two speech models and corrected against the script. For the fellowship showcase three weeks later, a five-minute pre-recorded version followed. Links: [Pitch deck (web)](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/iceland-north-route-site/biopath-ecef/)
- 21 Sep 2026 · **‘From strawberry patch to PhD’** (「从草莓田到博士」) — Published. The University of Bristol Careers Service published a Student Founder Spotlight on 21 September 2026 — ‘From strawberry patch to PhD: how engineering maths inspired BioPath’ — telling the story of a PhD researcher in Engineering Mathematics building a trap-placement optimisation tool for pest control: from its origin in a strawberry patch, through New Enterprise and the Early Career Enterprise Fellowship, to the Festival of Enterprise. Links: [Careers blog](https://universityofbristolcareers.blogs.bristol.ac.uk/2026/09/21/from-strawberry-patch-to-phd-how-engineering-maths-inspired-biopath/)

## 08 媒 Signal · 信号

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/media/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/media/

A camera roll kept since 2023, a WeChat studio launched in August 2026, LinkedIn as a public notebook, a home-built bilingual subtitle pipeline — and the long making-of of the site you are reading.

_Fig. 8 — A camera roll as the record of where the walk actually went._

- May 2023 · **Light painting, 2023** (光绘，2023) — Completed. In May 2023 a portfolio of light-painting photographs came together: long exposures in which a moving light draws paths that accumulate on the sensor over several seconds. It is the direct ancestor of this site's central image — a dark plate on which the paths of thousands of walkers accumulate into light.
- 25 Jul 2023 – 20 Sep 2024 · **Five headlines in fourteen months** (十四个月，五个头衔) — Completed. LinkedIn's email footers keep a quiet record of the profile's one-line headline: ‘student in Tianjin University’ in July 2023; a day later, ‘Applied Math Student @Tianjin University // Transforming Complexity into Simplicity’; then the same with a line seeking UK summer internships; then back to the plain applied-maths student; and from 20 September 2024, ‘Engineering Mathematics Student @University of Bristol’. That last one has not changed since — not for the PhD, the fellowship or the company role. This site is, in part, the overdue headline update. Links: [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zhouyixiaoxiao/)
- Sep 2023 – Aug 2026 · **A camera roll as a diary: 3,947 videos** (把相机胶卷当日记：3,947 段视频) — Completed. An inventory of the personal camera roll in August 2026 counted 3,947 videos shot between 3 September 2023 and 27 August 2026 — 140 in 2023, 1,310 in 2024, 1,574 in 2025 and 923 in 2026 up to August. Month by month, the counts trace the seasons of a life: quiet stretches, and surges whenever a new city or a new project began. Only these aggregates are published; the clips themselves stay private. They are the raw material for the WeChat studio. Metrics: Videos 3,947; By year (2023 · 2024 · 2025 · 2026) 140 · 1,310 · 1,574 · 923.
- Oct 2024 – Sep 2026 · **LinkedIn as a public notebook** (把领英当作公开的笔记本) — Ongoing. Until this site, LinkedIn was the de facto public page: the QR codes on the enterprise poster and on the ambassador posters point there, and so, for most of 2026, did zhouyixiaoxiao.com. Its posts are the milestones — starting the PhD, the enterprise fellowship, the festival pitch. The profile had 888 followers at an April 2026 snapshot. Metrics: Followers (Apr 2026 snapshot) 888. Links: [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zhouyixiaoxiao/)
- 3 Oct 2024 · **A first personal website** (第一个个人网站) — Published. On 3 October 2024 a LinkedIn post announced a first personal website, built a few months after the Tianjin maths guide. Its launch essay was a small personal credo: real freedom exists within constraints, and a game is most fun just beyond your comfort zone. Read again now, it describes a random walker in a bounded box. The address you are reading spent most of 2026 as a redirect to LinkedIn; this site is the third attempt.
- Nov 2025 · **Food philosophy, PhD edition** (饮食哲学·博士版) — Published. A LinkedIn post set out a ‘food philosophy, PhD edition’ as an optimisation problem: stay reliably fed without leaving the office too often. Two objectives — speed (under fifteen minutes a meal, often under ten, because other work runs in parallel while a potato is in the microwave) and cost — and one hard constraint: nutrition must be complete, macro and micro. It is a joke, and it is also exactly how everything else on this site gets decided.
- 21 Nov 2025 · **‘Starting a new position as PhD Student’** (「开始新职位：PhD Student」) — Published. On 21 November 2025 a one-line LinkedIn post shared the news: ‘I'm happy to share that I'm starting a new position as PHD Student at University of Bristol!’ — and the profile photo changed the same evening. A small post for a long walk: the PhD it announced is Chapter 01. Links: [The post](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7397674266298806273/)
- Feb 2026 · **Announcing the fellowship** (宣布成为创业学者) — Published. A LinkedIn post in February 2026 announced the appointment as a University of Bristol Early Career Enterprise Fellow for 2026, describing the PhD research on random walks and first-passage phenomena on graphs, and how it can inform decisions under uncertainty — the same mathematics that became BioPath.
- 9 Feb 2026 – 15 Feb 2026 · **Ink wash with a single red** (一抹朱红的水墨) — Completed. Two vertical images made with AI image generation under close art direction: a Chinese ink-wash landscape with a red sun, a pagoda, cranes, deer and a lone boat, made as a red-envelope cover in February 2026, and a remix with red lanterns and a gate for the Lunar New Year. Monochrome ink and a single vermilion accent — the palette this site is built on.
- 10 Jun 2026 – 27 Aug 2026 · **A home-built bilingual subtitle pipeline** (自己搭的中英双语字幕流水线) — Shipped. The local build of ffmpeg shipped without a subtitle renderer, so subtitles took another route: every bilingual cue is rendered as a transparent image and overlaid, in chunks of about ninety seconds processed in parallel — roughly twenty times faster, with an 8 min 44 s 4K clip rendered in about two and a half minutes. A native Swift tool followed in July, and caption rules in August: at most two lines, 18 Chinese or 46 English characters per line, zero overlaps, and a terminology audit.
- 29 Aug 2026 – 24 Sep 2026 · **‘First-Passage Universe’: the first prototype of this site** (「首达时宇宙」：这个网站的第一版原型) — Completed. The first design for this site, in August 2026, was a canvas of eight artboards: a particle-field hero, a prologue, a memory galaxy, a two-trajectory timeline, a digital twin and a research page. Reopened a month later, it earned a blunt verdict — no feeling of light and gradient, and no way to see the achievements — and a sharper brief followed: disruptive, playful, deeply artistic, strongly interactive, and a real summary of everything so far. The luminous plate on the front page, with the achievements beside it, is the answer.
- 29 Aug 2026 · **A WeChat content studio** (微信内容工作室) — Launched. In August 2026 an AI-assisted studio was set up to turn years of phone footage into short videos for WeChat Channels (视频号) and a WeChat Official Account (公众号). Four goals frame it: map every video in the archive; build a voice and a digital presence with clear AI disclosure; profile the speaking style and suggest how to improve it; and semi-automate publishing — with the final ‘publish’ click always made by a person. The transcription route is chosen and the pipeline is built; the topic map, and a ‘memory galaxy’ for this site, come next.
- 29 Aug 2026 – 31 Aug 2026 · **Finding the speech in 3,947 videos** (在 3,947 段视频里找到说话声) — Completed. A resumable background pipeline exported each video, extracted its audio, deleted the intermediate file and ran voice-activity detection, all under an adaptive disk budget on a machine short of space. Over about thirty-six hours it processed 3,943 of the 3,947 videos with no outstanding failures, and flagged 1,052 as containing speech. Only these counts are published; the speech itself includes other people's voices and stays private. Metrics: Videos with speech 1,052.
- 28 Sep 2026 · **This site: First Passage, Nº 01** (本站：首达 · 第 01 号) — Nº 01 · live. The site you are reading, in its first edition: a live first-passage experiment in which walkers leave Tianjin and search a luminous plate of 2021 to now for whatever you choose to measure. It replaces the page that, since April 2026, simply forwarded zhouyixiaoxiao.com to LinkedIn. It was designed and built with a large team of AI agents working to one specification, with every fact drawn from a verified, privacy-tagged record — and nothing private shipped.

## 09 行 Westward · 向西

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/westward/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/westward/

Summer 2025: a university programme in Silicon Valley and a two-week research internship at LiveX AI, where the question was how to turn messy manuals into Markdown an AI can actually use. The hinge of the turn toward AI — and a walker that is still walking.

_Fig. 9 — The one walker that has not been absorbed yet._

- 28 Jun 2025 · **Before: a CV sent twice in nine minutes** (之前：九分钟里发出两版简历) — Applied. The earliest step of the summer is a CV emailed on 28 June 2025 to apply for Tianjin University's Silicon Valley programme — followed nine minutes later by a revised version. Everything westward starts with that small, slightly anxious double send.
- 21 Jul 2025 – 25 Jul 2025 · **HKUST Engineering summer camp** (港科大工学院夏令营) — Selected. Selected for the HKUST School of Engineering's 2025 Summer Camp for Elite Students (21–25 July), a camp for prospective research postgraduates that included a visit to the Hong Kong Science Park. The first days in Hong Kong led straight on to the Bay Area — the opening of a three-city summer: Hong Kong, Silicon Valley, Bristol.
- 24 Jul 2025 – 16 Aug 2025 · **Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Program** (硅谷创业项目) — Completed. About three weeks in the Bay Area in the summer of 2025 on Tianjin University's Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Program — the Xuanhuai School's ‘Stanford & Silicon Valley’ programme, run with Founders Space, a San Francisco venture builder, for a cohort of about twenty students. Arriving late from the Hong Kong camp, the weeks filled up with a design-thinking workshop, visits to Silicon Valley companies, a symposium at Stanford and evening founder-and-investor meetups — and, inside the same window, a research internship at LiveX AI.
- 26 Jul 2025 · **A Saturday at Stanford Memorial Auditorium** (斯坦福纪念礼堂的一个周六) — Attended. The first weekend after landing in San Francisco meant a student ticket for the Saturday session of the Asian American Scholar Forum's Pioneer Medal Symposium and Ceremony at Stanford Memorial Auditorium, 26 July 2025 — the opening frame of the whole Bay Area chapter. Links: [Asian American Scholar Forum](https://www.aasforum.org/)
- 27 Jul 2025 – 30 Jul 2025 · **Design thinking: getting lost lights a beacon** (设计思维：迷路即点灯) — Team concept. In the first week on site the cohort took a Stanford-style design-thinking workshop, with the worked example ‘new students feel lost at Stanford’. Group 3's bilingual write-up turned getting lost into a feature: every wrong turn lights a community beacon and reveals a hidden story. It proposed four ‘bridges’ — E-ink beacon tags for leaving notes, a story-card deck whose AR clues unlock only on site, a sculpture projecting a live heat-map of wandering, and Bluetooth guide beacons carried by senior students — and scored wandering paths as ‘Bravery Points’. A random walk rewarded for wandering: the idea turns up again on this site.
- 4 Aug 2025 – 16 Aug 2025 · **LiveX AI — Researcher (Internship)** (LiveX AI——研究实习) — Completed. Role: Researcher (Internship). About two weeks, 4–16 August 2025, as a research intern at LiveX AI, a Bay Area start-up whose AI helps consumer companies with customer support, retention and growth. The brief: find the most reliable way to turn product manuals and customer documents into clean, structured Markdown for the company's support knowledge base. The work ran from a survey of document parsers and a six-dimension quality rubric to a vendor compliance matrix for the engineering team, and ended in a retrieval-based benchmark that judges parsers by whether their output actually answers questions. CV line: LiveX AI — Researcher (Internship), Aug 2025.
- 5 Aug 2025 · **A week in: an essay about a ladder in the clouds** (一周之后：关于云中天梯的随笔) — Completed. About a week into the programme came a six-part Chinese reflection of roughly 1,700 characters: a night arrival and a ride with a driver who lived in his car; the Pacific coast and a quiet Stanford campus; walking into the campuses of the big technology companies; conversations with investors and founders; and dawn over the Alviso salt flats. It ends on motivation — everyone stands on a different rung of a ladder wrapped in cloud, so just take your own next step.
- 5 Aug 2025 – 8 Aug 2025 · **Week one: nine PDFs and a six-dimension rubric** (第一周：九份 PDF 与一套六维量表) — Completed. The first week was a sprint: an investigation note on parsing benchmarks and popular tools, four converters run over nine representative test PDFs the same evening, and a written comparison the next day. When the engineering team asked for numbers and one more tool, a fifth was added, and by the end of the week a first deck scored the leading options from 0 to 10 on six dimensions — structural fidelity, formatting accuracy, special content, cleanliness, ease of post-processing and automation readiness. A follow-up request for something runnable set up the benchmark of week two.
- 11 Aug 2025 – 16 Aug 2025 · **An open retrieval-QA benchmark for document parsers** (一个开源的文档解析检索问答基准) — Shipped. The internship's study became an open benchmark in its final week. Each parser's Markdown is treated as a knowledge base and judged by downstream usefulness rather than visual fidelity: the text is chunked, the best passages are retrieved, a model answers only from what was retrieved — and may say ‘not found’ — and every answer is scored by exact matching and then by a rubric judge. Wrong answers given with confidence are tracked separately as overconfidence. Five parsers, nine documents, a hundred questions per document: 900 questions for every parser. Metrics: Parsers × documents × questions 5 × 9 × 100.
- 3 Sep 2025 – 9 Jan 2026 · **After: the summer, written into LinkedIn** (之后：那个夏天写进了领英) — Completed. The summer entered the public record twice: a ‘Researcher’ position at LiveX AI, added to LinkedIn in late August 2025 shortly after the internship; and, about five months later in January 2026, a ‘Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Program Participant’ entry at Tianjin University, added as the profile turned toward enterprise. What came after the summer is still in motion; on the plate it is the walker that has not yet been absorbed. Links: [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zhouyixiaoxiao/)

## 10 作 Workshop · 作坊

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/workshop/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/workshop/

Things built in the gaps: a maths guide for the next cohort, a travel-story studio born at a hackathon, a cursor that jumps between screens, bridges that let AI agents hand work to each other — most of them made so that someone else could move faster.

_Fig. 10 — A year of commits drawn as a walk; each shipped project an absorbing target._

- 1 Dec 2021 · **On GitHub since December 2021** (2021 年 12 月起的 GitHub) — Ongoing. The GitHub account dates from 1 December 2021. For three years it was quiet — coursework, a maths guide, a template — and then, in 2026, it erupted: most of the repositories were created that year, along with nearly all of the contributions, including a two-day spike when an automated agent factory built a hackathon product. The live counts on this page are fetched from GitHub at build time. Company work in private repositories is not counted, so the graph is a lower bound, not the whole output. Links: [GitHub profile](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao)
- 22 Jul 2023 – 18 Dec 2025 · **The Tianjin University maths guide** (天津大学数学学院本科生指北) — Live. Instead of only using the curriculum, write a guide to it for everyone who comes after. Built from July 2023, the Tianjin University maths undergraduate guide gathers what a student needs — a foreword, the professional courses, the majors and how to contribute — first as a quick guide with a document library, then as a MkDocs site. It has been served at zhouyixiaoxiao.info since December 2025 and is the oldest thing on this page that other people still use. Links: [zhouyixiaoxiao.info](https://zhouyixiaoxiao.info/)
- 21 Aug 2023 – 22 Aug 2023 · **TJU_Draw: shapes you can drag and rotate** (TJU_Draw：可以拖拽与旋转的图形) — Completed. A Windows drawing application written in C++ with MFC for the Tianjin University School of Mathematics computer practicum: draw lines, circles, ellipses, squares, rectangles and triangles, change stroke and fill colours, then drag, scale and rotate the shapes to any angle. The earliest interactive graphics in this collection — the plate on the home page is a distant descendant. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/TJU_Draw)
- 29 Nov 2024 · **A Tianjin University letterhead in LaTeX** (天津大学公函版式的 LaTeX 模板) — Published. A bilingual XeLaTeX template that reproduces Tianjin University's letterhead style — TJU blue, a logo slot, a contact block — written during the PhD application season for reference letters, then published so that anyone else applying could use it too. It was announced on LinkedIn twenty-five minutes after the repository was created. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/reference-letter-Tianjin-university-tju)
- 17 Feb 2026 – 14 Jul 2026 · **An always-on agent host, and an honest uninstall** (一台 7×24 在线的智能体主机，以及一次坦然的卸载) — Completed. A spare laptop became an always-on host for an open-source autonomous agent framework, driven from a phone through ordinary chat apps to run coding and browser tasks, with multi-agent channels, scheduled digests and an automated development loop for the SocialOS codebase. About two months of real use surfaced where autonomous agents break today: authentication churn, reliability when nobody is watching, and permissions that sprawl. The whole setup was uninstalled in July 2026 — the experiment was the point.
- 1 Mar 2026 – 9 Mar 2026 · **UK AI Agent Hack at Imperial** (帝国理工 UK AI Agent Hack) — Took part. Took part in the week-long UK AI Agent Hackathon EP4, which opened on 1 March 2026 at Imperial College London — and shared the call with the SEMT PhD community the day before. The entry was SocialOS, submitted to five bounty tracks at once; the public repository keeps the pitch pack, the architecture and the evidence documents. Links: [SocialOS repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/openclaw-foundry-socialos)
- 5 Mar 2026 – 9 Mar 2026 · **SocialOS: 1,222 commits in five days** (SocialOS：五天，1,222 次提交) — Completed. SocialOS turns raw notes, voice memos, screenshots and encounters into structured memory about people and events, ‘self-mirror’ reflections and drafts for each platform, delivered through a publishing queue that a human approves. It runs only on the local machine. It was built for the UK AI Agent Hack in five days, with 1,222 commits between 5 and 9 March 2026 — 1,084 of them carrying an ‘[autodev]’ prefix from the automated agent factory orchestrated for the week. The public repository keeps the pitch pack and the evidence. Metrics: Commits in five days 1,222; Made by the agent factory 1,084. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/openclaw-foundry-socialos)
- 7 Mar 2026 – 10 Jun 2026 · **Open-source agent skills** (开源的智能体技能包) — Shipped. A public, sanitised collection of reusable skills and setup kits for coding agents — mail access, security-minded skills and a portable configuration template — plus small utilities for AI desktop apps. The larger personal library stays private; what is published is what anyone can safely reuse. Links: [Skills collection](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/codex-skills-public-collection)
- 15 Mar 2026 · **Why the browser's voice input went deaf** (浏览器的语音输入为什么「聋」了) — Published. A bilingual repository that diagnosed why voice input failed in the ChatGPT Atlas browser — it stored its own audio-input priority and preferred an external monitor's microphone over the built-in one — and ships an audit script and a reversible fix that reorders the priority, plus a userscript that keeps video speed controls on ordinary sites. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/chatgpt-atlas-voice-video-speed-fix)
- 1 Apr 2026 – 8 Apr 2026 · **A route site for a snowy Iceland drive** (为冰岛雪路自驾做的路线站) — Completed. In April 2026, a self-drive around Iceland's ring road, along the south coast and through the East Fjords to Akureyri, with a stop in Oslo. For one snowy leg — Bakkagerði to Akureyri by Route 94, Mývatn, Húsavík and Goðafoss — a public Chinese route-decision site laid out A, B and C options with links to the official road conditions. Planning a trip like a product, again. Links: [Route site](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/iceland-north-route-site/)
- 18 Apr 2026 – 19 Apr 2026 · **Global HackTour London: one city, three cuts** (Global HackTour 伦敦站：一座城，三种剪辑) — Took part. At the in-person Global HackTour London at UCL on 18–19 April 2026, built ‘London Cuts — One City, Three Cuts’: upload a London memory and get back a story in three narrative modes — Punk, Fashion, Cinema — along with a collectible postcard and a pin on a story atlas. The weekend prototype became the London Cuts product. Links: [Hackathon repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/London-Hackthon)
- 19 Apr 2026 – 28 Apr 2026 · **London Cuts** (London Cuts 旅行故事工作室) — Live demo. A creator tool for documenting a single-place trip with photos grounded in their own metadata, written stories and AI-generated postcards in six styles, switchable between three visual modes — Fashion, Punk and Cinema — with public reader pages, a map atlas and PDF or PNG export. The live demo tells ‘A Year Around London’ in thirteen stops and ‘A Week in Reykjavík’, and it has entry points for AI agents too: an llms.txt, an OpenAPI description and an MCP endpoint. London Cuts is a working name. Links: [Live demo](https://london-cuts.vercel.app) · [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/london-cuts)
- 26 Apr 2026 – 27 Apr 2026 · **A fashion-editorial housing map** (时装杂志风的租房地图) — Live. A single-page map for incoming Chinese LLM students at Bristol: seventeen student housing options within about a twenty-minute walk of the Law School, each tagged by how its information was sourced — verified, provider, search or live — with an application section, a mobile detail panel and an offline basemap fallback. Built in a weekend, with an editorial look borrowed from fashion magazines. Links: [The map](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/bristol-llm-housing-map/) · [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/bristol-llm-housing-map)
- 29 May 2026 – 30 May 2026 · **CatchMouse, rebuilt for Apple Silicon** (为 Apple Silicon 重写的 CatchMouse) — Shipped. A clean Swift rewrite of CatchMouse, an Intel-only utility from 2011: a menu-bar agent that warps the cursor to the left, centre or right display with global hotkeys, cycles between displays, remembers custom hotkeys per monitor, flashes display numbers and offers command-line verbs. It builds a universal app with only the command-line tools and needs no accessibility permission. MIT-licensed. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/CatchMouse)
- 9 Jun 2026 – 10 Jun 2026 · **Seven dead ends and a working ⌘T** (七条死路与一个能用的 ⌘T) — Published. A small Swift helper, about 200 lines, that registers ⌘T only while the ChatGPT Atlas browser is in front and routes it to Claude — switching to an existing tab, duplicating it or opening a new one — through the accessibility interface. The README is the fun part: it documents why seven standard approaches fail, because the browser's new-tab page is a native view rather than a web page. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/atlas-claude-tab)
- 27 Jun 2026 – 29 Jun 2026 · **Pro Agent Bridge** (Pro Agent Bridge 智能体桥) — In daily use. A local MCP server that turns ChatGPT's developer mode into a bounded coding and hand-off surface for one repository: reading files, searching, exact edits, git inspection and safe verification commands. It extends the MIT-licensed open-source CodexPro by rebel0789 with hand-off from ChatGPT Pro to Claude Code, saved-session capture and hardened polling, and it is still in daily use. Credit where it is due: the foundation is upstream. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/pro-agent-bridge)
- 22 Sep 2026 · **A legal-career roadmap for Bristol LLM students** (给布里斯托法学硕士的法律职业路线图) — Live. A responsive, editorial-style Chinese guide for Bristol LLM students planning a legal career back in China in 2026–27: chapter navigation, full-text search, filterable events and recruitment, a four-week practice plan, ten copy-ready templates, dated updates on official AI products and 42 primary sources — with no analytics and no backend. The same editorial language as the housing map: a small shelf of Bristol guides. Links: [The guide](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/bristol-law-career-roadmap/)

## 11 学 Roots · 来路

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/roots/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/roots/

Tianjin, Hong Kong, Chengdu, Geneva, Bristol: a maths degree with an oar in hand, an exchange year that turned the maths computational, a first internship, and the 3+1 route — the first shortcut, which skipped a year.

_Fig. 11 — Six cities joined by a random walk, and the 3+1 jump that skipped a year._

- 2021 · **Self-Improvement Award, Tianjin University** (天津大学北洋自强奖) — Awarded. Received Tianjin University's Self-Improvement Award (北洋自强奖) in 2021, the first year of the degree — a small badge at the very start of the walk.
- Aug 2021 – Jun 2025 · **Mathematics and Applied Mathematics, Tianjin University** (天津大学数学与应用数学) — Completed. Entered the School of Mathematics at Tianjin University in the 2021 cohort, in an honours mathematics class, reading Mathematics and Applied Mathematics until June 2025 — analysis, advanced algebra, real and complex analysis, mathematical modelling — and qualifying for exemption from the national postgraduate entrance exam. The final stage was completed at the University of Bristol through the 3+1 route. On the plate, Tianjin is the origin: every walker leaves from here.
- Sep 2021 – Jun 2023 · **Rowing for Tianjin University** (天津大学赛艇队) — Completed. Rowed for the Tianjin University rowing team from September 2021 to June 2023, taking second place in the mixed 2000 m at the 4th Tianjin Water Sports Games and cutting a personal 500 m time by about fifteen per cent over the two years. A physical rhythm under the mathematics: stroke, recover, repeat.
- 24 Dec 2021 · **Darboux's theorem and Hilbert's third problem** (达布定理与希尔伯特第三问题) — Completed. Two end-of-term essays for the first-year special-topic courses in analysis and algebra, both dated 24 December 2021: ‘Darboux's theorem’, seven pages on why a derivative cannot jump, and ‘Hilbert's third problem’, fifteen pages on whether any two polyhedra of equal volume can be cut into matching pieces. The first long-form mathematics.
- 2022 · **A certified personal trainer, too** (顺便，是一名持证私教) — Certified. Earned the NSCA Certified Personal Trainer credential in the winter of 2022, out of an interest in training and fitness. It is an unexpected line on a mathematician's record — and perhaps why the lunch-optimisation post treats complete nutrition as a hard constraint.
- 2022 · **Outstanding Student Cadre** (天津大学优秀学生干部) — Awarded. Recognised as an Outstanding Student Cadre of Tianjin University in 2022, for the student-leadership work of the first two years — the thread of service that later reappears in Bristol as a PGR representative.
- Aug 2022 – Sep 2022 · **Guiding a hundred new mathematicians** (带一百多名新生入学) — Completed. Led a team of three freshmen class guides supporting more than a hundred incoming mathematics students through August and September 2022 — campus tours, answering questions, and acting as the link between new students and staff. A year later, the same instinct produced the maths guide.
- Sep 2022 – Jun 2023 · **Head of Student Rights, School of Mathematics** (数学学院学生会权益部部长) — Completed. Led the Student Rights department of the Tianjin University School of Mathematics student union from September 2022 to June 2023, taking more than forty student issues on accommodation and facilities to resolution and setting up more than twenty conversations between students and the school's administration. It was the first time representing other students — and the role came back, three years later, in Bristol.
- Nov 2022 – Sep 2025 · **The 3+1 route: the first shortcut** (「3+1」：第一条捷径) — Completed. The degree's final stage ran through the Tianjin University–University of Bristol 3+1 route: three years at Tianjin — the third spent on exchange in Hong Kong — then the one-year MSc at Bristol. Selection came in November 2022; by September 2024 the move was made. The bachelor's (to June 2025) and the master's (from September 2024) overlap, which is why the plate draws this as a shortcut: a long-range jump that skips a year.
- Sep 2023 – Jun 2024 · **An exchange year at HKUST** (港科大交换的一年) — Completed. Spent the 2023–24 academic year as an exchange student at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, taking partial differential equations, numerical solution of PDEs and applied statistics. It was where the mathematics turned computational — and where a first neural-network research project began.
- Sep 2023 – May 2024 · **Tianjin University's booth at HKUST** (在港科大为天大摆展位) — Completed. While on exchange, ran an information booth representing Tianjin University at HKUST, telling visiting students in English and Chinese about research, collaboration and exchange opportunities — an ambassador before the title existed.
- Nov 2023 – 31 May 2024 · **Physics-informed neural networks for PDEs** (用物理信息神经网络解偏微分方程) — Completed. A research project at HKUST from November 2023 to May 2024 used physics-informed neural networks in PyTorch to solve partial differential equations — one-dimensional diffusion, a two-dimensional wave equation and Laplace's equation in two and three dimensions — comparing uniform and random sampling of the training points. The 22-page report, ‘Using PINN to solve diffusion, wave and Laplace equations’, is dated 31 May 2024. It is the earliest point on the thread from mathematics to AI.
- Jul 2024 – Sep 2024 · **Research intern, JLL Chengdu** (仲量联行成都研究部实习) — Completed. Role: Research intern. A research internship in the Chengdu research department of JLL (Jones Lang LaSalle) in the summer of 2024, through the Sichuan–Hong Kong summer internship programme, joined while on exchange at HKUST: data-driven market research, collecting and cleaning large retail datasets in Python, and turning them into findings for stakeholders. The programme's visits — Guang'an, the Sanxingdui Museum, the panda base — made it a month of Sichuan as well as spreadsheets.
- Jul 2024 – Aug 2024 · **A first press mention, in Chengdu** (第一次见报，在成都) — Completed. During the summer internship programme of 2024, a visit to the Chengdu World Horticultural Expo on 23 July ended up in a local news report that quoted by name. Around it came speeches at the opening and closing ceremonies of the summer programme for university students — a first stage, and a first microphone. Links: [News report (Chinese)](https://static.cdsb.com/micropub/Articles/202407/bdcc0db02c8f048d477d9f8ce896f0ed.html)
- Sep 2024 – Sep 2025 · **MSc Engineering Mathematics, University of Bristol** (布里斯托大学工程数学硕士) — Completed. Moved to Bristol in September 2024 for the MSc in Engineering Mathematics. The modules ran from statistical computing and empirical methods, information theory and coding, and renewable energy to mathematical modelling in biology, medicine and public health, methods of AI, and skills in mathematical research. It finished with a Distinction and a dissertation on first passage — see Chapter 01.
- Sep 2024 – Sep 2025 · **Night shifts as a Student Warden** (学生公寓的值班 Warden) — Completed. During the MSc year, worked part-time as a Student Warden in Bristol student accommodation: duty shifts giving residents frontline support and responding to fire alarms under the safety procedures, with fire-warden training completed in December 2024.
- Jan 2025 – May 2025 · **What makes a flight late?** (航班为什么会晚点？) — Completed. In a five-person MSc team project with an industry partner in logistics, led the synthesis of more than fifteen causal-inference papers and applied structural causal models to an aviation dataset of about 29,000 points, isolating the effect of weather on delays while controlling for latitude and season. The team combined the causal analysis with Kolmogorov–Arnold networks.
- 8 Feb 2025 – 17 Feb 2025 · **Geneva: a UN field-exchange programme** (日内瓦：联合国实地交流项目) — Completed. A winter study programme in Geneva built around the UN Office at Geneva, 8–17 February 2025 — WFUNA's Youth Training Program at the UN, with workshops on humanitarian affairs, multilateralism, diplomacy and the Sustainable Development Goals. In a thirty-person simulated UN conference, represented Australia and led the drafting of a fifteen-minute script for a vaccine-cooperation conference; the group visited WIPO, the ILO, the FAO, UNODA, CERN and the IFRC.
- Mar 2025 · **Three languages, one of them at A1 for now** (三种语言，其中一种暂时停在 A1) — Completed. Mandarin Chinese is native, English is at IELTS 7.0 and French is at A1. In practice the working life is bilingual by default: talks, papers, documentation and websites — this one included — usually ship in English and Chinese at once, and one research paper is about what happens when people type to AI in the space between the two.
- 27 May 2025 · **BSc thesis: epidemics in heterogeneous spaces** (本科论文：异质空间中的疾病传播) — Completed. The Tianjin University undergraduate thesis, completed in May 2025 at 117 pages, couples confined lattice random walks with local SIR epidemic dynamics in a reaction–diffusion framework and derives a closed-form basic reproduction number for heterogeneous spaces. It is tested in four indoor settings — an office, a supermarket, a classroom and a metro car — and a spectral decomposition makes each evaluation millisecond-scale, roughly four orders of magnitude faster than Monte Carlo. The random walk was already there before the PhD.
- Jun 2025 · **Graduating from Tianjin University** (天津大学本科毕业) — Graduated. Completed the Tianjin University BSc in Mathematics and Applied Mathematics in June 2025, while already in the final months of the Bristol MSc through the joint route — two degree bars closing within three months of each other.
- Sep 2025 · **MSc with Distinction** (硕士以 Distinction 毕业) — Completed. The MSc in Engineering Mathematics at the University of Bristol was awarded with Distinction in 2025. Two months later the same school became the home of the PhD — the walker stayed in the box, and went deeper.

## 12 今 Now & Next · 此刻

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/now/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/now/

As at the build date: a poster to present in Edinburgh, a paper submitted to Physical Review E and another in preparation, a desktop agent in development, a new teaching year and a second year as PGR rep. The walkers still in flight.

_Fig. 12 — Walkers still in flight, as at the build date._

- 24 Nov 2026 – 25 Nov 2026 · **UKAIRS 2026, Edinburgh** (UKAIRS 2026，爱丁堡) — Scheduled · 25 Nov 2026. The UK AI Research Symposium runs on 24–25 November 2026 at the John McIntyre Conference Centre in Edinburgh, and the poster is up on Wednesday 25 November. The plan, written into the paper: a side-by-side demo showing, for each task, the native prompt, its keyboard-friendly variant, the agent's response, the grade and the effort estimate — so that visitors can toggle from routine prompts to exact-term stress prompts and watch where meaning collapses. Chapter 02 of this site is a first draft of that demo. Links: [Poster list](https://ukairs2026.eventsadmin.com/i/PosterSessions)
- 30 Jul 2026 · **Geometry-controlled folds — submitted to Physical Review E** (几何控制的折叠——投稿 Physical Review E) — Submitted to Physical Review E, Jul 2026. ‘Geometry-controlled folds of first-passage-time bimodality under localized absorption’ was submitted to Physical Review E as a single-author regular article on 30 July 2026. It is the first paper of the PhD and the capstone of the double-peak line: the geometry of a localized absorber decides whether a second arrival peak exists at all, and the peak is lost through a saddle-node fold whose location can be computed exactly. Every figure on this site that shows the effect is generated by our own simulations, not taken from the manuscript. Links: [Research atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/)
- 23 Sep 2026 · **Programmable multimodality — manuscript in preparation** (可编程多峰——稿件准备中) — Manuscript in preparation. ‘Programmable multimodality and saddle-node loss of reaction-time peaks under a fixed catalyst budget’ is a single-author manuscript in preparation. A fixed amount of static catalyst, split into thin stripes along the path of a reacting Brownian pair, programs the reaction-time density: at weak noise each stripe removes a fixed fraction of the arriving pairs — a stick-breaking law — so there is exactly one peak per stripe, and designs with prescribed peak times and weights exist, are locally unique and can be found by Newton's method. Fixed-width stripes can instead lose a late peak through a saddle-node bifurcation, certified by interval arithmetic in test cases. The finite-dimensional and calculus core is checked in Lean 4; the stochastic parts are proved by hand. Links: [Reproduction archive](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes)
- 8 Sep 2026 – 26 Sep 2026 · **prescribed-reaction-time-modes: a public reproduction archive** (prescribed-reaction-time-modes：公开复现仓库) — Live. Everything behind the fixed-budget paper is public and checkable: simulation, analysis and plotting code, machine-readable numerical records, interval-arithmetic certificates, the Lean 4 sources and the Isambard 3 job records, each tied to SHA-256 manifests. Five releases went out between 8 and 26 September 2026 as the paper was rebuilt — about 1,466 files in the latest, including 100 Python scripts, 27 Lean files and 1,198 JSON records. Anyone can re-run the numbers without asking. Metrics: Releases 5 (v1.0.0 → v1.3.0); Files in v1.3.0 ≈ 1,466. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes) · [Release v1.3.0](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes/releases/tag/v1.3.0)
- 11 Aug 2026 · **What the next version will measure** (下一版要测什么) — Planned. What comes next: position the work against related research; match the title to the zh-CN evidence; soften the design rule to fit the small homophone samples; run a small typing study, so that both sides of the effort–quality trade-off are measured rather than modelled; build about thirty homophone tasks with graded ambiguity to trace a real performance curve; pin every model version; and look harder at why ‘normalise first’ hurts. The eight-language harness is ready for the broader claim.
- 9 Jun 2026 · **Scaling to eight scripts** (扩展到八种文字) — Planned. The next study was built before a single call was spent: 44 tasks across eight languages (264 prompt variants), split into high-risk exact-script tasks and controls; a fixed matrix of frontier models; a statistics engine with paired bootstrap confidence intervals; and generators for every table and figure. An adversarial audit from eight native-fluency perspectives replaced four homophone pairs that did not truly collapse. The main run is waiting on a go/no-go decision, so there are no multilingual results yet — and none are claimed. Metrics: Tasks · languages · variants 44 · 8 · 264.
- 23 Sep 2026 · **From chat window to desktop agent** (从聊天窗口到桌面智能体) — In development. The desktop assistant is becoming a coding and office agent: an open-source agent engine underneath, a YueXin interface on top. Before the change, three domestic models were shown to complete real coding tasks through the company gateway. The next rounds add quota requests, governance telemetry, a web agent with sandboxed code execution, web search and file reading, a built-in browser, and acting in Feishu on the person's behalf — with a confirmation before every send, share or approval — plus a diff panel and terminal, scheduled tasks, skills and plugins. Telemetry is metadata only, and every employee can see all of it on a ‘My data’ page.
- Jun 2026 · **AI lead (R&D), Yuexin International** (阅信国际 AI 负责人（研发）) — Ongoing. Role: AI lead (R&D). From June 2026, alongside the PhD, AI lead (R&D) at Yuexin International (阅信国际), a cloud-communications company working across messaging, voice and AI. The brief has three parts: the company's AI platform and model gateway; its AI transformation — moving teams from trying AI to working with it every day; and AI support for the international messaging business. The entries below are what got built. Links: [Yuexin International on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/yuexin-international)
- 16 Jul 2026 · **2026–27: thirteen roles across three schools** (2026–27：三个学院，十三个岗位) — Ongoing. The initial 2026–27 allocation covers thirteen teaching roles across eleven units in three schools. In Mathematics: Perspectives in Data Science and Perspectives in Mathematics, support sessions for Theory of Inference, marking for Quantum Computation and a tutorial group for Introduction to Pure Mathematics. In SEMT: demonstrating and marking for Engineering Mathematics 1, group supervision in Mathematical and Data Modelling 3, labs in Statistical Computing and Empirical Methods, and Foundations of AI. In CADE: AI-Driven Design and Simulation, and the group research project of the new MSc in Engineering with AI. A Linear Algebra tutorial group was added in September. Metrics: Teaching roles 13; Units 11; Schools 3.
- 18 Aug 2026 · **A returning rep for 2026–27** (连任 2026–27 学年代表) — Ongoing. Bristol SU confirmed a second year as the Engineering Mathematics PGR Academic Rep on 18 August 2026. The new year began with helping bring new PhD reps into the team and keeping the School's PhD community space open to newcomers; the faculty rep forums resume in November.
- 29 Aug 2026 · **A WeChat content studio** (微信内容工作室) — Launched. In August 2026 an AI-assisted studio was set up to turn years of phone footage into short videos for WeChat Channels (视频号) and a WeChat Official Account (公众号). Four goals frame it: map every video in the archive; build a voice and a digital presence with clear AI disclosure; profile the speaking style and suggest how to improve it; and semi-automate publishing — with the final ‘publish’ click always made by a person. The transcription route is chosen and the pipeline is built; the topic map, and a ‘memory galaxy’ for this site, come next.
- 3 Nov 2025 · **PhD in Engineering Mathematics, University of Bristol** (布里斯托大学工程数学博士) — Ongoing. Role: PhD researcher. The PhD began on 3 November 2025 in the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology (SEMT) at the University of Bristol. The subject is first-passage time: how long a random walker takes to reach a target for the first time, and why the distribution of that time can split into two peaks. Over the first year the work has broadened to span stochastic processes and the evaluation of AI agents. The random walks moving across this page are the same kind of object the thesis studies.
- 28 Sep 2026 · **This site: First Passage, Nº 01** (本站：首达 · 第 01 号) — Nº 01 · live. The site you are reading, in its first edition: a live first-passage experiment in which walkers leave Tianjin and search a luminous plate of 2021 to now for whatever you choose to measure. It replaces the page that, since April 2026, simply forwarded zhouyixiaoxiao.com to LinkedIn. It was designed and built with a large team of AI agents working to one specification, with every fact drawn from a verified, privacy-tagged record — and nothing private shipped.
